'''''Polemonium caeruleum''''', known as '''Jacob's-ladder'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=17 October 2014 }}</ref> or '''Greek valerian''', is a hardy [[Perennial plant|perennial]] flowering plant. The plant produces cup-shaped, blue or white flowers. It is native to [[temperate climate|temperate]] regions of Europe. It is the [[type species]] of the phlox family, [[Polemoniaceae]].

==Growth==
The plant usually reaches {{convert|45-60|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall and broad, but some occasionally grow taller than {{convert|90|cm|in|abbr=on}}. It can grow in North American [[hardiness zone]] 2.

==Habitat==
The plant is native to damp grasslands, woodlands, meadows and rocky areas in temperate areas of Europe and northern Asia.<ref name=MOBOT>{{cite web |title=''Polemonium caeruleum'' |url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=a796 |website=Missouri Botanical Gardens |accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
The plant normally prefers soil that is rich in moisture and lime with partial shade. Normally hardy, some [[cultivar]]s (e.g. 'Blue Pearl') behave as tender [[biennial plant|biennials]], which means they are effectively annuals in cooler climates (below [[hardiness zone]] 6).

The plant is known to have a few landscape uses as well such as attracting beneficial insects. The plant itself is convenient for container planting due to the shape of its growth. The flower may be presented as a cut flower or foliage and may be added to bouquets for its pleasant smell. It can be grown in a perennial border or rock garden.<ref>{{cite web |title=School of Horticulture Plant Database |url=https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/plant/plantDetail/1002 |publisher=Kwantlen Polytechnic University |accessdate=10 November 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161110235547/https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/plant/plantDetail/1002|archive-date=10 November 2016}}</ref>

Cultivars include:
* 'Album' (white flowered)
* 'Blue Pearl'
* 'Brise d'Anjou'
* 'White Pearl' (white flowered)
* 'Snow and Sapphires' (variegated foliage)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.paghat.com/jacob.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031013125045/http://www.paghat.com/jacob.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=October 13, 2003 |title='Snow & Sapphire' Variegated Jacob's Ladder |publisher=Paghat the Ratgirl |accessdate=11 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url = http://www.terranovanurseries.com/articles/american_gardner_DEC_06_1.pdf |title=From Backyard to Big Time |journal=The American Gardener |first=Doreen G. |last=Howard |publisher=American Horticultural Society |volume=85 |issue=6 |page=17 |year=2006 |accessdate=10 May 2016}}</ref>

The plant does not have serious insect or disease problems. [[Leaf spot]] and [[powdery mildew]] can be problems, particularly in humid climates. The foliage may scorch if the plant gets too much sunlight. The [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflet]] tips will brown if soils are allowed to dry out. The foliage will generally decline and become less attractive as the summer progresses. It is important to keep an eye out for slugs.<ref name=MOBOT />

==Other uses==
''Polemonium caeruleum'' was voted the [[County flowers of the United Kingdom|county flower]] of [[Derbyshire]] in 2002 following a poll by the wild plant conservation charity [[Plantlife]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantlife.org.uk/wild_plants/county_flowers |publisher=Plantlife |title=County Flowers |accessdate=19 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130806080053/http://www.plantlife.org.uk/wild_plants/county_flowers |archive-date=6 August 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
